steps.text: Preheat the oven to 350 degrees F (175 degrees C).
Place butter in a 9x13-inch baking dish and melt butter in the oven. Remove the dish when butter is melted, about 3 minutes.
Beat eggs in a large mixing bowl. Mix in flour, milk, and baking powder until combined. Mix in cheese, spinach, and onion. Spoon mixture into the buttered baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven for 35 minutes. Let cool for 45 minutes, then cut into bite-sized squares.

raw_recipe.headline: Spinach Cheese Squares
raw_recipe.description: These baked cheesy spinach squares are easy to make with eggs, Cheddar, onion, and frozen spinach for a savory party appetizer.
raw_recipe.name: Spinach Cheese Squares

review.reviewBody: I love this recipe; just remember to use medium cheddar or it’s too bland... I also make Greek spinach squares by using feta cheese instead of cheddar and adding ½ tsp of dried dill.

These turned out great for my Christmas Eve buffet of finger food. I did add some Tabasco and used less cheese (only because I don't know how to measure a pound of cheese, LOL). Nuke the spinach for a few minutes right in the box, then press it through a colander to drain the water.

Be sure to squeeze the water from the spinach. I just rubbed the pan with butter from the stick before pouring the batter into the dish. I sometimes add a 4th egg to increase amount and it comes out fine. I also sometimes use almond flour for a gluten free version and it comes out great. Serve either warm or cold. Always a hit when I serve these squares.

I have been making this recipe for about 50 years, and it never fails to be extremely popular! I'm not a spinach fan but love these. People need to remember to squeeze all the liquid out of the thawed spinach, and I use sharp cheddar.

These were SO GOOD! Reminded me of what my grandma used to make for Christmas! I added one more egg, 2 teaspoons of ground mustard & 1 teaspoon of Lawry’s season salt-because even with the cheese, it needed more salt. Can’t wait to make again.??????

super easy and great recipe.. I decided to use fresh spinach, so remember that for fresh spinach it will take 4-5 times the amount of fresh amount of spinach called for in the recipe. So I sautéed down about 24 oz of raw spinach to end up with close to 10oz of cook spinach and then cut the recipe in half to match the amount of cooked down spinach I had. Also, remember to let the spinach cool and then squeeze out as much of the water as you can before weighing it and adding it to the recipe. I love how this turned out.
It doesn't say to defrost and squeeze the spinach dry. ?

I’ve been making almost this exact recipe for 20 years or more. Difference is mine calls for 1 teaspoon of salt, and I add 1/2 teaspoon of black pepper. I’ve changed up the cheese too, sometimes. My favorite is pepper jack, but you could use Monterey jack too. I’m making it today. I used half sharp cheddar and half pepper jack. Whatever I’ve used it’s always been yummy. Try it cut into small squares as an appetizer with cocktails.
Came out firm, moist and tasty; added a couple pinches of garlic powder for a little kick and shredded taco cheese blend and cheddar cheese blend 👍🏻

Very simple recipe but a bit bland without some adjustments. I did add 1 tablespoon chopped red onion, a clove of minced garlic and a pinch of cayenne pepper. Very tasty and will be a wonderful appetizer for guests.

I tried to follow the recipe as much as I could but I exchanged the frozen spinach with LOTS of fresh from the garden and put extra spices in it, baked for 40 minutes then put extra cheese across the top and browned it under the broiler. Huge success. I will be making it again. Soon. 😂 Addition. I have decided not to put the extra cheese on the top again. It was good when it was still hot but once it cooled down it was too chewy for the dish.
Quick recipe that you can make for a gathering. Everybody always loves these and sadly I never have any leftover. No worries I'll make more for myself. Thanks for sharing - been making for years.
I've been making a similar recipe for years but it includes sauteed mushrooms. Believe me, it takes it over the top!
The original recipe from a long time ago does have 1 tsp of salt. I think it was omitted by mistake. It also called for 1/2 Cup diced red bell pepper.

The recipe is amazing. I substituted the cup of flour with a cup of cottage cheese. I mix my cheeses. I used extra sharp cheddar. With a quarter of cup of pecorino Romano two large garlic cloves, crushed two green onions and one medium size shallot. And it is amazing. I eat them as breakfast squares.
I didnt have baking bowder replaced 1 cup flour to half and half bisquick. mm

Loved mixing two cheeses (pepper jack too) and it was great. I can’t believe people DID NOT read the areas in directions/ingredient that says spinach must be thawed and drained!! I pressed mine in a colander and used a towel. Next time I’ll try adding salsa or hot sauce.
I use 1/2 cheddar and 1/2 pepper jack. Also, I use one pack frozen/ thawed spinach and one bag cut broccoli. Delicious! We have made this and devoured it several times!

These were very good, but needed a little flavor boost. Maybe a dash of hot sauce and some garlic, salt, and pepper. I added the extra egg, as some suggested, and I think that was necessary. All in all, a convenient and tasty recipe that needs some flavor tweaks.
This is really good if you love spinach, plus a little salt and 5 eggs instead of 3 makes a big difference
